_note: All words shown by lineup.js live here. 'ui' strings are keyed placeholders; {name} is filled in by the script. 'facts' cite keys in sources.json. Molecule names and sizes come from lineup-data.json (built from the structure files).

ui.title: Size lineup
ui.badge: True scale: every molecule drawn from its real structure file
ui.vsWater: {x} times as wide as a water molecule
ui.isWater: The smallest one here: the yardstick for the rest
ui.atomsThin: {n} atoms in the file, 1 in every {s} drawn
ui.assembly: Measured on the whole molecule as the viewer builds it
ui.tapHint: Tap a molecule to see its size. Tap it again to open it. Drag or scroll sideways to walk the line.
ui.viewAria: Molecules lined up from smallest to biggest at true scale
ui.keys: Left and right arrows step from molecule to molecule. Enter opens the chosen one. Plus and minus zoom, 0 shows them all, Home and End jump to the smallest and biggest.
ui.how: Each size is the widest distance between the centres of any two atoms in the molecule's structure file, the same file the molecule viewer opens. Proteins and DNA come from X-ray crystal structures, which usually leave out hydrogen atoms, so their real outline is a little bigger. Small molecules use the ideal shape from the chemical component dictionary, hydrogens included. Each drawing is the molecule turned so its longest side stands up, flattened onto the screen. Big molecules are drawn with fewer atoms, each one a little larger, so the outline stays solid.
ui.alt: A row of {n} molecules standing side by side on one line, smallest on the left and biggest on the right, all drawn at the same true scale as coloured dots, one per atom. On the left, water is a speck {water} nm across. Small food and body molecules such as glucose and caffeine are under a nanometre. Proteins grow from a few nanometres to more than 10, and the biggest, {biggest}, is {big} nm across, about {ratio} times as wide as water.
ui.loadFail: The lineup data could not be loaded.

facts.t: Every size on this page is measured from the same structure file the molecule viewer opens.
Small molecules come from the PDB's chemical component dictionary; big ones are crystal structures from the Protein Data Bank.
